referenceRole: The original M uniformly enlarged on its original reference canvas; sole image input for every call.
generationPolicy: One letter per sequential Fgen invocation; inspect the saved output before starting the next. Each call references only the original M. No raster warping, thresholding, contour repairs, vector substitutes or automatic selection from retries.

N.prompt: Image 1 is my ORIGINAL uppercase M and the ONLY style reference. Generate exactly ONE new letter: uppercase N, as a sibling drawn by the same type designer. Do not redraw M or use any previously generated letter. Preserve the M's soft asymmetric silhouette, broad rising ribbon versus narrower returning strokes, gently flowing edges, rounded crests, tight smooth inner turns and rounded-flat terminals. Make an unmistakable printed uppercase N: two tall gently forward-leaning upright stems connected by one descending diagonal from the upper left to the lower right. Both outside stems must reach the cap line and baseline. Keep broad rising stems, a narrower diagonal return, smooth tight connected joins and softly cut feet. Leave the upper-right and lower-left spaces clearly open. No arch or closed bowl: not M, H, lowercase n or a separate zigzag symbol. Interpret this anatomy in the original M's ribbon language, not as a generic bold italic sans-serif or a uniform-width rounded font. Use a solid white filled glyph on a pure black square background, at approximately the same cap height and baseline placement as the supplied M. Only the letter N: no M, other characters, words, labels, grids, guides, outlines, shadows or texture. Keep the entire glyph inside the canvas with generous black margins.
